headline: Moderate El Nino -- RONI +1.36 degC (JJA 2026; legacy ONI +1.80), power index 78/100 (Very High), intensifying rapidly.
episode_status: El Nino conditions present for 3 consecutive seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC; 2 more needed before NOAA logs this as a formal episode.

notes: 4 candidate analogs were dropped for being too dissimilar to the current trajectory.

alerts.title: Legacy ONI and official RONI diverging
alerts.detail: ONI +1.80 against RONI +1.36, a gap of +0.44 degC. That much of the raw anomaly is the whole tropical ocean running warm rather than the Pacific, which is why CPC has classified on RONI since February 2026.

outlook.label: South of Southern Mexico
outlook.text: 1. South of Southern Mexico: An area of low pressure could form late this week or this weekend to the south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter, environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development while the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward. Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

outlook.label: Invest 93W
outlook.text: THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 93W)PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 15.4N 155.0E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 15.9N 152.8E, APPROXIMATELY 494 NM EAST-NORTHEAST OF GUAM. ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED (EIR) SATELLITE IMAGERY DEPICTS A MOSTLY OBSCURED LOW LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER WITH DEEP FLARING CONVECTION ALONG THE WESTERN PERIPHERY. ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS REVEALS A FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR DEVELOPMENT WITH STRONG POLEWARD UPPER-LEVEL OUTFLOW, LOW VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (10-15 KTS), AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (29-30 C). GLOBAL DETERMINISTIC MODELS GENERALLY AGREE ON 93W CONTINUING TO CONSOLIDATE AS IT TRACKS WESTWARD. OUT OF THE ENSEMBLE MODELS, ECENS IS THE MOST AGGRESSIVE REGARDING NEAR-TERM DEVELOPMENT. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 18 TO 23 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1007 MB.THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS IS UPGRADED TO HIGH. SEE REF B (WTPN21 PGTW 291700) FOR FURTHER DETAILS.

stormfury.verdict: 7 of 7 live storms fail STORMFURY's own criteria. Every one of them fails on supercooled water, which is the criterion no hurricane has ever passed and the reason the programme ended.
reasons: TRIGGER: the seeding agent needs supercooled liquid water and hurricane eyewalls are already glaciated at seeding altitude. Nothing to freeze, so the mechanism never starts. Willoughby et al., Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc., 1985.

MAGNITUDE: across 27 natural eyewall expansions in 9 hurricanes this season, conserving angular momentum predicted a mean 27.7% wind drop and the storms actually gave up 4.3%, overstating it 6.4-fold. A hurricane is fed high-momentum air continuously, so a closed-system argument is an upper bound, not a forecast. STORMFURY's predicted effect came from that same calculation.

DETECTION: 17 of 215 unseeded hurricane intervals this season weakened by at least the 31% STORMFURY claimed for Debbie, and 39 moved that far in one direction or the other. An effect that size is indistinguishable from what hurricanes do untouched, which is what closed the programme.

programme.agencies: US Weather Bureau / NOAA with the US Navy

seeded_storms.name: Esther
seeded_storms.outcome: Flown before STORMFURY formally existed, as the proof of concept that got the programme funded.

seeded_storms.name: Beulah
seeded_storms.claimed: eyewall dissipated and reformed further out
seeded_storms.outcome: The first run missed the target area entirely. The second produced the reformation the hypothesis predicted, which is also what an unseeded eyewall replacement looks like.

seeded_storms.name: Debbie
seeded_storms.outcome: The showcase: five seedings on each of two days. These are the numbers the programme is remembered for, and the ones the natural replacement cycle later explained without any silver iodide.

seeded_storms.name: Ginger
seeded_storms.outcome: A large, diffuse storm with no coherent eyewall to move. It was seeded because it was what was available, which is itself a statement about how rarely the criteria above are met.

atlas.method: Past El Ninos (RONI >= +1.0) minus neutral years (|RONI| < 0.5), per season, per grid cell, since 1979, with each event and each neutral year counted once. Welch's t accompanies every difference and is judged against each season's own 95% point of Student's t. An event under way when the grids were built is left out.

cpc_discussion.synopsis: El Nino is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter 2026-27.
cpc_discussion.body:
El Nino strengthened further over the past month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +3.0°C in the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Except for the Nino-4 index, which decreased to +0.1°C in August, values in the other Nino indices increased, reaching +1.8°C in Nino-3.4, +2.5°C in Nino-3, and +3.4°C in Nino-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) remained steady during August [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline [Fig. 4] . Subsurface temperatures continued to be significantly above average, with widespread anomalies in excess of +10.0°C at depth. Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies extended from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices remained negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Nino.

The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Nino will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . During the October-December 2026 season, there is a 75% chance of a historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Nino events dating back to 1950 (+2.5°C or more for a 3-month RONI value ). With an event of this magnitude, the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Nino are larger, though not guaranteed (see CPC outlooks for probabilities of seasonal anomalies). In summary, El Nino is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter 2026-27.
